subject: Integration Handoff: SDK & Endpoint Migration for LumenPay
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@lumenpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenPay Implementation <impl@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Kickoff + handoff for LumenPay app integration

Hi Evelyn / Monica —

Thanks for the intro. We (LumenPay) are ready to kick off the implementation for the payments UX that will call Redwood for payment-chat assist and a lightweight embedding lookup. Our engineering lead (cc'd as impl@) will take technical handoff next week. Before the call, could you send any digestible docs we should review (SDK setup, recommended timeouts/retry patterns, and the planned endpoint migration if we move from the sandbox to prod)?

High-level constraints:
- Production SLA: 99.5% for critical payment flows (low-latency target <120ms median token latency).
- Traffic profile: bursty spikes during payroll windows (up to 12k requests/minute peak).
- Security: we need IP allowlist guidance and the SOC2 checklist for audit.

Can we get a short checklist + one-page runbook for the engineer to follow during the first 48h? Attachment: sample data mapping attached on our side.

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Liu
Head of Integrations | LumenPay
[attachment: lumenpay-kickoff-data-mapping.csv (csv)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff + handoff for LumenPay app integration

Samantha — thanks, welcome!

We're attaching a concise 48h checklist and a short SDK snippet pack that covers Node/Python examples and a migration checklist from sandbox -> prod. High-level plan:
1) Day 0-1: SDK install, auth check, simple generate/test vector calls.
2) Day 1-2: Implement retries/timeouts, prefix caching for embeddings, and set up rate-limit backoff.
3) Day 2-4: Load testing at expected bursts, adjust batching and autoscaling signals.

I've attached: lumenpay-integration-checklist.xlsx and redwood-sdk-sample-snippets.md. Also sharing our allowlist doc (networking-and-ip-allowlist.pdf).

Action: Diego (solutions engineer) will send concrete code for token retry/backoff and endpoint migration steps. Monica will confirm rate-limit thresholds and recommended throttling settings for Dedicated pools.

Propose a 45-min technical handoff call: Tue 2026-11-23 15:00 PT — does that work?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[attachment: lumenpay-integration-checklist.xlsx (xlsx), redwood-sdk-sample-snippets.md (md), networking-and-ip-allowlist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@lumenpay.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff + handoff for LumenPay app integration

Samantha — quick note on rate limits and autoscaling knobs you'll want in config: 

1) Client-side: set a concurrency cap of 50 connections per process for the initial rollout. Add a shared token bucket if you have multiple processes.
2) Server-side autoscaling signals: burst allowance of 2x baseline for 3 minutes, then scale if sustained. We'll map this to Dedicated pool sizing if you choose reserved capacity.
3) Batching: for embeddings, batch up to 512 vectors or ~16kb payloads per request depending on vector size. This minimizes head-of-line latency but increases throughput efficiency.

We can provide a simple middleware snippet for Node/Python that enforces these rules and exposes a /health endpoint showing token bucket status for dashboards.

-Monica
Sr. Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Liu <samantha@lumenpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, LumenPay Implementation <impl@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff + handoff for LumenPay app integration

Thanks, Diego / Monica — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our eng lead: 
- For socket timeouts, you recommend 6-10s; in our payments flow we prefer failing fast at 1.5s and falling back to a cached reply. Should we implement a two-tier timeout (1.5s fast-fail + background longer retry)?
- On batching for embeddings: we plan to parallelize uploads across 4 workers during off-peak. Do you see any problems with that approach and the token bucket recommendation?

On the call tomorrow we'll share sample traffic logs. Also: any quick note on cost controls we should enable at prod switch?

Samantha

Samantha — quick reply from the commercial side:

We'll approve a small integration credit (1 month of token usage capped at $5k) for your initial canary and load testing phase. Evelyn will follow up with a brief amendment and next steps for procurement if you want Dedicated sizing.

On timeouts: the two-tier approach (1.5s fast-fail + background retry) is a common pattern we recommend for payment-critical paths. Make sure the background retries do not double-submit side-effecting operations; prefer idempotency keys.

I'll be on the handoff call and can confirm credits/order-of-operations there.

Thanks — Ben
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
